user_query: I need an object detection model to locate people, dogs, and cats in indoor and outdoor photographs. The objects may appear at different scales, under varied lighting, and may be partially occluded by furniture or other people. The model will run locally on a MacBook Air with an Apple M4 chip and 16 GB of unified memory, using Metal acceleration where supported. It should aim for a mAP@0.5:0.95 of approximately 0.40 or higher and recall of at least 0.75 for each class. Processing an image within roughly 500 milliseconds would be desirable.
use_case_description: Object detection to locate person, dog, cat in indoor and outdoor photographs.

available_hardware.details: Apple Silicon MacBook Air; Metal acceleration available; 16 GB unified memory.

applicable_rules.rule_name: Choose smaller YOLO variant for latency-first use
applicable_rules.adjustment_value: Prefer nano or small variants before larger variants within the same YOLO family.
applicable_rules.notes: Inferred from official benchmark tables where smaller variants generally have lower latency/compute; use as a suggestion rather than a hard rule.

applicable_rules.rule_name: Choose larger YOLO variant for accuracy-first use
applicable_rules.adjustment_value: Consider medium, large, or xlarge variants if hardware and latency budget allow.
applicable_rules.notes: Inferred from official benchmark tables where larger variants generally have higher mAP50-95; use as a suggestion rather than a hard rule.

applicable_rules.rule_name: Use a conservative batch size for limited training memory
applicable_rules.notes: A batch size of 4 is a conservative local policy for an 8 GiB training-memory budget and works consistently on CUDA and MPS, where Ultralytics AutoBatch is not reliable. The threshold and batch size are application policy rather than an upstream benchmark setting.

applicable_rules.rule_name: Consider increasing image size for accuracy-first use
applicable_rules.adjustment_value: Consider increasing image size if hardware allows and validation performance improves.
applicable_rules.notes: Partly supported by image size being a configurable training/prediction parameter that affects compute; this is a tradeoff rule, not an explicit Ultralytics prescription.

applicable_rules.rule_name: Consider reducing image size for latency-first use
applicable_rules.adjustment_value: Consider reducing image size if latency or compute is more important than accuracy.
applicable_rules.notes: Partly supported by image size being a configurable training/prediction parameter that affects compute and latency; this is a tradeoff rule, not an explicit Ultralytics prescription.

applicable_rules.rule_name: Consider YOLOv10 for NMS-free low-latency detection
applicable_rules.notes: Supported by YOLOv10 documentation describing NMS-free inference and latency-oriented motivation; actual speed depends on deployment hardware and export format.

applicable_rules.rule_name: Maximize mosaic and imgsz for tiny objects
applicable_rules.notes: Forces network to train on artificially smaller objects without losing resolution.

applicable_rules.rule_name: Increase weight_decay and HSV for overfitting
applicable_rules.notes: Penalizes large weights to force generalization and reduces memorization of colors.

applicable_rules.rule_name: Increase warmup_epochs for early NaN loss
applicable_rules.notes: Allows random initial weights to settle gently before full learning rate kicks in.

applicable_rules.rule_name: Set close_mosaic for clean final predictions
applicable_rules.notes: Disables heavy spatial augmentations in the final 10 epochs for clean bounding boxes.

applicable_rules.rule_name: Decrease augmentation for massive datasets
applicable_rules.notes: Prevents underfitting when natural dataset variance is already extremely high.

applicable_rules.rule_name: Increase max_det for crowded environments
applicable_rules.notes: Bypasses the hardcoded 300-object limit in default NMS logic.

applicable_rules.rule_name: Enable early stopping to save compute
applicable_rules.notes: Prevents wasting GPU hours on a model that has stopped improving. Standard heuristic is patience=50 when epochs=100 to 300.

applicable_rules.rule_name: Set YOLO HSV augmentation for outdoor lighting variation
applicable_rules.notes: Ultralytics shows this exact custom augmentation example and describes HSV shifts as useful for outdoor/lighting and camera variation.

applicable_rules.rule_name: Use 10-degree YOLO rotation augmentation for orientation variation
applicable_rules.notes: Ultralytics documents degrees=10.0 as an exact example that samples rotations between -10.0 and 10.0 degrees and states rotation is crucial when objects appear at different orientations.

applicable_rules.rule_name: Use YOLO scale=0.5 for object distance and size variation
applicable_rules.notes: Ultralytics documents scale=0.5 as the default and states it samples final scale factors from 0.5 to 1.5 to handle objects at different distances and sizes.

applicable_rules.rule_name: Use YOLO CutMix probability 0.5 for occlusion-heavy scenes
applicable_rules.notes: Ultralytics documents cutmix=0.5 as an exact example and states CutMix helps recognize objects when partially occluded by other objects.

applicable_rules.rule_name: Disable YOLO mosaic for the final 20 epochs of a 200-epoch run
applicable_rules.notes: Ultralytics states that with epochs=200 and close_mosaic=20 mosaic is disabled after 180 epochs; mosaic=1.0 means the transform is always applied before close_mosaic disables it.

applicable_rules.rule_name: Set YOLO single-class training for object-presence-only datasets
applicable_rules.notes: Ultralytics documents single_cls as treating all classes in multi-class datasets as a single class during training.

applicable_rules.rule_name: Set YOLO rectangular batching for efficiency on varied aspect ratios
applicable_rules.notes: Ultralytics documents rect=True as minimum padding to a common size and states it can improve efficiency and speed but may affect accuracy.

applicable_rules.rule_name: Set YOLO multi-scale training to +/-25 percent
applicable_rules.notes: Ultralytics documents multi_scale=0.25 as varying image size from 0.75x to 1.25x each batch.

applicable_rules.rule_name: Set YOLO inference batch above 1 for offline directory inference
applicable_rules.notes: Ultralytics documents inference batch default 1 and states larger batch size can provide higher throughput for directory/video/list sources.

applicable_rules.rule_name: Prefer efficient video-friendly detectors for traffic surveillance
applicable_rules.notes: UA-DETRAC establishes real-world traffic video detection and tracking as the domain context; YOLO evidence should be used to select a speed-oriented detector variant.

applicable_policies.guidance: Choose the largest hardware-safe micro-batch. For classification, use gradient accumulation only when needed to reach a moderate effective batch; effective_batch=batch_size*gradient_accumulation_steps*gpu_count. Never exceed training_hardware.max_batch_size. Preserve a grounded recipe optimizer by default. For Ultralytics optimizer='auto', do not claim control of learning_rate because Ultralytics derives and overrides it. A grounded recipe or a specifically justified LLM decision may instead select a supported explicit optimizer; in that case choose learning_rate jointly with effective batch size and treat linear batch scaling as a starting heuristic, not a mandatory formula.

Choose epochs from dataset size and transfer-learning mode. Smaller datasets may need more epochs but earlier stopping. Keep patience below num_epochs, warmup a small fraction of training, and leave enough post-warmup epochs for learning.
Keep architecture-required resolution fixed. Otherwise favor larger inputs for small-object/accuracy priorities and smaller inputs for memory or latency pressure, within recipe and runtime bounds.

Freezing is valid only with pretrained weights. For YOLO, freeze is the number of initial layers kept frozen for the whole run, not a number of epochs. For a small dataset with explicitly supported similarity to the pretraining domain, start with freeze=10 (current train_images=4800); with uncertain similarity use 0-5, and with strong domain shift, ample data, or training from scratch use 0. Treat these as validation experiments, not correctness rules. TorchVision trainable_backbone_layers has different semantics and must not be translated mechanically.

Use moderate geometry and color augmentation for box detection, scaled to dataset size. Keep semantically unsafe flips/color shifts conservative. Do not enable mask-only copy-paste for box-only data, and close mosaic before the final epoch.

Treat these as safe starting values, not calibrated optima. Favor higher max_detections and less aggressive suppression only when crowded-scene evidence exists; respect NMS-free architectures. Final thresholds should be calibrated on validation data.

applicable_policies.guidance: Choose the largest hardware-safe micro-batch. For classification, use gradient accumulation only when needed to reach a moderate effective batch; effective_batch=batch_size*gradient_accumulation_steps*gpu_count. Never exceed training_hardware.max_batch_size. Preserve a grounded recipe optimizer by default. For Ultralytics optimizer='auto', do not claim control of learning_rate because Ultralytics derives and overrides it. A grounded recipe or a specifically justified LLM decision may instead select a supported explicit optimizer; in that case choose learning_rate jointly with effective batch size and treat linear batch scaling as a starting heuristic, not a mandatory formula.

Choose epochs from dataset size and transfer-learning mode. Smaller datasets may need more epochs but earlier stopping. Keep patience below num_epochs, warmup a small fraction of training, and leave enough post-warmup epochs for learning.
Keep architecture-required resolution fixed. Otherwise favor larger inputs for small-object/accuracy priorities and smaller inputs for memory or latency pressure, within recipe and runtime bounds.

Freezing is valid only with pretrained weights. For YOLO, freeze is the number of initial layers kept frozen for the whole run, not a number of epochs. For a small dataset with explicitly supported similarity to the pretraining domain, start with freeze=10 (current train_images=4800); with uncertain similarity use 0-5, and with strong domain shift, ample data, or training from scratch use 0. Treat these as validation experiments, not correctness rules. TorchVision trainable_backbone_layers has different semantics and must not be translated mechanically.

Use moderate geometry and color augmentation for box detection, scaled to dataset size. Keep semantically unsafe flips/color shifts conservative. Do not enable mask-only copy-paste for box-only data, and close mosaic before the final epoch.

Treat these as safe starting values, not calibrated optima. Favor higher max_detections and less aggressive suppression only when crowded-scene evidence exists; respect NMS-free architectures. Final thresholds should be calibrated on validation data.

Given the performance requirements (mAP@0.5:0.95 around 0.40, recall per class ≥ 0.75, and ~500 ms per image), yolov10n offers the best balance of efficiency, capacity headroom, and verifiable benchmark performance among the shortlisted architectures while staying within the available hardware envelope. dataset_selection_decision_evidence.rationale: Selection strategy: use a single coherent training family (Open Images 2019 detection train) as the primary pool to maximize a shared backbone across all three target classes (person, dog, cat) and to align with general photography domain. Open Images provides very large per-class training pools and consistent detection annotations, enabling efficient sampling and stable training on a MacBook Air with Metal acceleration. Per-class allocations are set to 2,000 images, aiming for roughly 2k total per class (6k total training images across all classes in the patch) to meet the Medium accuracy/latency target without overfitting or excessive training time. This preserves the rule of selecting only from exact dataset IDs listed under each class (Open Images train) and uses the primary pool for all three classes, keeping class-pool ratios balanced (2k/2k/2k). The approach leverages the large, diverse Open Images coverage across indoor/outdoor scenes typical of photography workloads, and it leaves room to enrich with additional families (e.g., LVIS or COCO) later if higher recall or long-tail coverage is desired. Estimated final per-class pool size is ~2,000 images (training), with the total selected training pool around 6,000 images before validation/test splits; actual final splits will be determined by deterministic code. The default download budget appears modest relative to the available data and was not a limiting factor for this selection.

Deterministic baseline derived from GraphRAG: Yolov10_n (Nano, NMS-free) selected for its very low memory footprint and VeryLow latency, suitable for MacBook Air (M4) with Metal acceleration. Open Images-based training data provides broad indoor/outdoor coverage across the three target classes with balanced per-class allocations (~2000 each). To meet latency and accuracy targets, memory-aware adjustments were applied: batch_size reduced to 4 to fit the 8 GB training-memory budget; amp disabled to ensure stable training on Apple hardware; workers set to 4 to match hardware parallelism. The learning_rate remains at 0.01 under the auto optimizer policy; Ultralytics owns LR/momentum when optimizer=auto, so no explicit tuning is claimed. The final configuration preserves the base balanced YOLO fine-tune recipe and uses the predefined dataset allocations to aim for mAP@0.5:0.95 around 0.40 with per-class recall >= 0.75, while keeping runtime under the 500 ms target on typical consumer hardware. Added fallback rationales for: fliplr, freeze, lambda_box, lambda_cls, lambda_dfl, scale, translate, warmup_momentum.

used_policies.guidance: Freezing is valid only with pretrained weights. For YOLO, freeze is the number of initial layers kept frozen for the whole run, not a number of epochs. For a small dataset with explicitly supported similarity to the pretraining domain, start with freeze=10 (current train_images=4800); with uncertain similarity use 0-5, and with strong domain shift, ample data, or training from scratch use 0. Treat these as validation experiments, not correctness rules. TorchVision trainable_backbone_layers has different semantics and must not be translated mechanically.

Use moderate geometry and color augmentation for box detection, scaled to dataset size. Keep semantically unsafe flips/color shifts conservative. Do not enable mask-only copy-paste for box-only data, and close mosaic before the final epoch.

Model Selection Rationale: Based on the deterministic recommendation provided by the GraphRAG context, yolov10n is chosen as the architecture. It is a Nano-size, NMS-free variant with very low parameter count (~2.3M) and small memory footprint (~0.25 GB VRAM estimate). It achieves a COCO map50-95 of about 39.5 on 640 px input (close to the target 0.4 mAP@0.5:0.95) and demonstrates very low inferred latency on GPU backends (1.84 ms on T4 TensorRT FP16 in the benchmarks). The CPU latency is not measured in the provided data (unverified) and is estimated from model complexity, with a stated limit of 500 ms. This creates a practical risk boundary that yolov10n is likely to meet on a MacBook Air with an Apple M4 when using Metal acceleration, but the CPU path remains unverified. The deterministic recommendation explicitly lists yolov10n as the top-ranked executable candidate under the current constraints and notes no fallback model is defined (fallback_model = null). Given the performance requirements (mAP@0.5:0.95 around 0.40, recall per class ≥ 0.75, and ~500 ms per image), yolov10n offers the best balance of efficiency, capacity headroom, and verifiable benchmark performance among the shortlisted architectures while staying within the available hardware envelope. If CPU latency proves higher than desired during deployment, the graph indicates no formal fallback, but the closest next-best options with similar memory footprints are yolov11n, yolov12n, or yolov12s, which trade some latency for potential gains in accuracy on challenging scenes. For the current setup, yolov10n is the recommended starting point and a solid baseline to validate against real indoor/outdoor data with the target classes (person, dog, cat).”, Local constraint validation replaced the agent choice 'yolov10' with 'yolov10n'.

Data Selection Rationale: Selection strategy: use a single coherent training family (Open Images 2019 detection train) as the primary pool to maximize a shared backbone across all three target classes (person, dog, cat) and to align with general photography domain. Open Images provides very large per-class training pools and consistent detection annotations, enabling efficient sampling and stable training on a MacBook Air with Metal acceleration. Per-class allocations are set to 2,000 images, aiming for roughly 2k total per class (6k total training images across all classes in the patch) to meet the Medium accuracy/latency target without overfitting or excessive training time. This preserves the rule of selecting only from exact dataset IDs listed under each class (Open Images train) and uses the primary pool for all three classes, keeping class-pool ratios balanced (2k/2k/2k). The approach leverages the large, diverse Open Images coverage across indoor/outdoor scenes typical of photography workloads, and it leaves room to enrich with additional families (e.g., LVIS or COCO) later if higher recall or long-tail coverage is desired. Estimated final per-class pool size is ~2,000 images (training), with the total selected training pool around 6,000 images before validation/test splits; actual final splits will be determined by deterministic code.
